name: NIH Stroke Scale

version.label: NINDS NIH Stroke Scale (15 items)
version.detail: Item definitions per the NINDS scale (updated 2024). The optional distal motor item is not part of the total and is not included.

purpose: Standardised quantification of neurological deficit in acute stroke.
intendedPopulation: Adults with suspected or confirmed acute stroke, assessed by trained examiners.

inputDefinitions.label: 1a. Level of consciousness
inputDefinitions.help: A response must be chosen even if evaluation is limited (e.g. intubation, language barrier). 3 only if no movement other than reflexive posturing to noxious stimulation.

options.label: Not alert; arousable by minor stimulation
Not alert; needs repeated or strong stimulation
Reflex responses only, or totally unresponsive

inputDefinitions.label: 1b. LOC questions (month, age)
inputDefinitions.help: Only the initial answer is graded; no partial credit for being close.

inputDefinitions.label: 1c. LOC commands (eyes, grip)
inputDefinitions.help: Credit if an unequivocal attempt is made but not completed due to weakness. Only the first attempt is scored.

options.label: Forced deviation or total gaze paresis
options.detail: Not overcome by the oculocephalic manoeuvre.

options.label: Bilateral hemianopia
options.detail: Blind from any cause, including cortical blindness.

options.label: Minor paralysis
options.detail: Flattened nasolabial fold, asymmetry on smiling.

options.label: Partial paralysis
options.detail: Total or near-total paralysis of the lower face.

options.label: Complete paralysis of one or both sides
options.detail: Absent upper and lower facial movement.

resultStates.label: No deficit measured
resultStates.summary: No deficit measured on the NIHSS items at this assessment.
resultStates.detail: A score of 0 does not exclude stroke. Deficits outside the scale (e.g. gait ataxia, vertigo, isolated distal weakness) are not captured.

resultStates.label: NIHSS {total}
resultStates.summary: Higher scores indicate greater measured neurological deficit.
resultStates.detail: The NINDS scale defines no official severity categories, and bands used in studies differ. Interpret the item profile and the trend alongside imaging and the clinical picture.

clinicalInsights.text: Report the total with the item breakdown. Serial scores by the same method are more informative than a single value.
Language and articulation items contribute to the total. For a similar lesion size, left-hemisphere strokes tend to score higher than right-hemisphere strokes.
Extinction or inattention is present; neglect may affect the reliability of other items.
Low scores can still accompany disabling deficits; posterior circulation deficits in particular may be under-represented.

limitations: Weighted toward anterior circulation and language; posterior circulation strokes may score low.
Requires trained, certified examiners for reliability.
Item scoring follows strict instrument rules (e.g. first attempt only) that differ from routine examination.

limitations.text: {nt_count} item(s) untestable and contributing no points: the total may underestimate the deficit.

commonErrors: Coaching the patient or scoring the best rather than the first attempt (items 1b, 1c).
Scoring ataxia that is explained by weakness.
Marking items untestable for reasons other than those the instrument allows.
Scoring a pre-existing deficit as new without documenting it.
whatItDoesNotTellYou: Whether the deficit is due to stroke or a mimic.

guideSections.what: A 15-item examination quantifying neurological deficit after stroke; totals range 0–42.
guideSections.whenUseful: Initial assessment of suspected stroke, serial monitoring, communication between teams, and trial outcomes.
guideSections.howToCalculate: Administer items in order. Record what the patient does, not what you think they can do. Score each item immediately; do not go back. Use UN only where the instrument allows it and record the reason.
guideSections.clinicalContext: Treatment decisions use the NIHSS alongside imaging, timing and patient factors under local protocol.
